answer: An agent economy can blunt a Sybil attack with a stake-and-vouch quorum: each agent locks a bond and may cast a vote only after two already-bonded agents attest it is a distinct identity. A fake army must purchase and lock one bond per fake, and every vouch puts the backer's bond at risk of slashing once a duplicate surfaces, so the attacker's cost grows linearly with the number of fake identities, while honest validators simply mirror the prevailing stake tide and withhold trust from newcomers who wander in with no proven history.
